historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance-anchored FY2027-FY2028 base-case revenue growth (VOYXACT/SIMTRIYO/zipalertinib ramps net of JYNARQUE erosion). The equity 5yr CAGR of 10.4% is NOT used as the forward proxy: the FY2029-2031 REXULTI and ABILIFY MAINTENA US loss of exclusivity breaks the trend, and the base 10-year revenue CAGR is only ~2.3%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs (40.5% 3yr, 20.3% 5yr) and the owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (38.6%) diverge by far more than 30% from the equity CAGR (~10.5%): FY2022 was a trough year (EPS 247, FCF 104bn) and FY2024-FY2025 carried yen weakness (USD/JPY ~110 -> ~150), the FY2025 MicroPort gain and a cash-tax lag. Revenue (11.6-12.4%) is the cleaner series and is itself ~3-4pp FX-inflated.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs are FY2025 vs FY2022 (3yr) and FY2025 vs FY2020 (5yr), entirely inside the IFRS era; the FY2014 9-month stub and the J-GAAP/IFRS break at FY2015/16 are not spanned. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest and dividends received; SBC is zero): FY2020 125,811, FY2022 91,314, FY2025 243,154. Reported-FCF CAGRs are 36.1% (3yr) and 14.2% (5yr) -- owner and reported agree because SBC is nil; the gap is the interest/dividend strip only.

scenario_narratives.base: Three launches (VOYXACT, SIMTRIYO, zipalertinib) plus compounding royalties carry growth through FY2028, then the REXULTI/ABILIFY MAINTENA US loss of exclusivity produces a shallow FY2029-31 revenue dip (cumulative ~-1%) and a margin trough at 17% before a 2-3% mature recovery; pipeline-replacement spend is charged at 7% of revenue and the terminal multiple is capped at 15x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The launches scale to blockbuster size and ASIMTUFII/Japan hold the CNS franchise, so the LOE is a plateau; margins hold 21-22% and bolt-on spend eases to 6.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Launches disappoint, the yen strengthens, and the FY2029-31 LOE lands in full (-16% cumulative) with margins resetting to 14-15% while pipeline purchases continue at 7.5% of revenue; profitable and net-cash throughout.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Otsuka is valued as a stream of fully loaded owner cash flow: core operating EBITDA (ex equity-method profit, after impairments), less the full lease cost, less tax at the book rate, less PP&E, intangible AND bolt-on pipeline purchases at ~7% of revenue, less working capital consumed by growth; the equity-method investments and financial assets are added back at book because their income is stripped from the flows. The build deliberately models the FY2029-31 LOE as a dip rather than smoothing it, charges the pipeline-replacement treadmill as maintenance capex, and caps the terminal multiple at 15x so none of the value depends on a re-rating. Dividends (JPY 200/share FY2026, 27.7% payout) and buybacks are the channel through which that FCF reaches shareholders; they are not added on top.
key_risks_to_valuation: Timing and depth of REXULTI and ABILIFY MAINTENA US generic entry (modelled from ~2029): a two-year delay or a 30/70 rather than 70/30 erosion split is worth several hundred yen per share either way

Capex basis: charging bolt-on acquisitions as recurring (7.0% vs the 5.7% PP&E+intangibles-only basis of reported FCF) is ~1,200 yen/share of value; if the Transcend/Araris/ICU run was a one-off bulge, the base is too low
VOYXACT peak sales (IgAN market estimated USD 6-10bn) and label expansion -- the single largest swing between bull and base
USD/JPY and EUR/JPY: guidance rests on 158/185; every 10 yen of USD/JPY strength is roughly 4-5% of pharma revenue in translation
Equity-method investments (374.6bn) and other financial assets (273.1bn) are taken at book; a 25% haircut is ~300 yen/share
US drug-pricing and tariff policy, flagged by management in the Q3 FY2026 filing, could pressure the US-weighted CNS and oncology franchises before the LOE

data_sources.financials: 4578.T_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, IFRS from FY2016; FY2014 9-month stub and J-GAAP years excluded from all growth maths); balance sheet, share count and cash flow anchors from 4578.T_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt (30 Sep 2026) and 4578.T_Annual_FY2025.txt; FY2026 guidance from the 30 Oct 2026 Q3 filing and presentation (4578.T_Presentation_Q3-FY2026.txt).

inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero filer. No share-based payment add-back on the IFRS cash flow statement; statement of changes in equity shows 'Share-based payment transactions' of only JPY 0.5-1.1bn/yr (4578.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:866,894,928), i.e. <0.05% of revenue. Kept as an explicit 0% row; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 share buybacks JPY 70,096m (4578.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:1018); 9M FY2026 JPY 47,085m (4578.T_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt:967). Genuine repurchaser: shares outstanding fell 542.7m (FY2023) -> 523.9m (Sep-2026) with periodic treasury cancellations (4.54m more resolved 30 Oct 2026). Count held FLAT per house rule; because SBC is zero the buyback is a pure return of the FCF already credited, so the flat count is conservative rather than neutral.
inputs.share_count_basis: Shares issued 542,988,917 less treasury 19,081,004 = 523,907,913 at 30 Sep 2026 (4578.T_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt:112-116). No dilutive securities: 'Diluted earnings per share have not been stated given an absence of potential shares with dilutive effect' (4578.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:1225). Held flat; annual_share_growth_pct 0.
inputs.fy0_basis: FY2026 is the base year on the 30-Oct-2026 guidance (revenue JPY 2,725.0bn, operating profit JPY 488.0bn, business profit JPY 500.0bn). 9M actuals (revenue 2,042.4bn, OP 423.7bn) are 75% of the year and guidance has been raised three times in FY2026; two months remain at the valuation date, so FY2026 flows are treated as already in the balance sheet and Year 1 is FY2027. The 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet therefore omits roughly one quarter of FY2026 FCF less the Q4 dividend/buyback outflow -- a small, conservative mismatch.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z (TSE regular close, 30 Oct 2026; not an after-hours print)
inputs.net_debt_note: Bonds and borrowings 6,964 current + 87,062 non-current = 94,026; cash and cash equivalents 472,489 (4578.T_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt:635,666,677). Net cash 378,463. Lease liabilities (22,240 + 75,225 = 97,465) EXCLUDED because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). Other financial assets, equity-method investments, other financial liabilities and NCI are itemised in equity_bridge, not here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built: 10y JGB ~1.7% risk-free + 6.0% Japan/global ERP x beta 0.9 = ~7.1%, rounded to 7.0%; debt is <2% of capital so WACC ~ cost of equity. Beta 0.9 is the long-run systematic exposure of global large-cap pharma, not Otsuka's trailing ~0.5-0.6 (measured over a product-growth phase that does not contain an LOE). Same rate in all three scenarios: product-concentration, LOE, launch and FX risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and weights, never as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Lease principal repayments JPY 24,695m FY2025 (4578.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:1024), 9M FY2026 JPY 19,571m (~26bn annualised), plus ~JPY 2-3bn lease interest inside 'interest paid' = ~1.0% of revenue, charged via lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT. Lease liabilities excluded from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2026E total D&A ~122bn (9M 91,107 x 4/3) less ROU depreciation ~26bn = ~96bn = 3.5% of revenue, so the lease is not charged twice through the tax line.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI stock JPY 68,783m at 30 Sep 2026 (4578.T_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt:698) deducted once in equity_bridge; flows are consolidated. NCI share of profit is ~1.3% of group profit (4,357 of 326,463 in 9M FY2026), so an attributable-only leakage driver would be noise.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is CORE EBITDA = IFRS operating profit EXCLUDING share of profit of equity-method associates (non-cash, inside OP per 4578.T_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt:717) and excluding non-recurring gains, plus total D&A, AFTER impairment losses (pipeline write-offs are a recurring cost of the R&D model: 126bn FY2024, 26bn FY2025, 15bn 9M FY2026). FY0 anchor: FY2026 guidance OP 488 - associates ~45 + D&A ~122 = ~565bn = 20.7% of 2,725bn. Cross-check FY2025 actual on the same basis: OP 479.4 - MicroPort gain 52.6 - associates 33.7 + D&A 116.2 = 509.3bn = 20.6%. Management's 'business profit' (JPY 500bn FY2026, 18.3% margin) includes associates and excludes impairments/other income; it is referenced in narrative only.
inputs.capex_basis: capex_pct_path carries PP&E PLUS intangible-asset purchases PLUS bolt-on pipeline acquisitions, because for a pharma facing serial LOEs these are maintenance spend, not optional growth. Actuals: FY2024 PP&E 95.6 + intangibles 33.8 + subsidiaries 115.6 = 245bn (10.5% of revenue); FY2025 87.8 + 53.8 + 87.3 = 229bn (9.3%) (4578.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:1007-1011); 9M FY2026 76.5 + 132.7 (incl. ~117.6bn Transcend/TSND-201) + 1.3 = 210.5bn (10.3%) (4578.T_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt:956-960). Base charges 7.0% (PP&E ~3.5% + pipeline purchases ~3.5%), below the Transcend/Araris/ICU-inflated 3-year run but well above the 5.7% PP&E+intangibles-only figure the reported FCF uses. Each 1pp of capex is ~JPY 30bn/yr of FCF, roughly JPY 900-1,000/share -- this and the LOE path are the two inputs that matter most.
inputs.working_capital_basis: Manufacturer/distributor: receivables 578bn + inventories 414bn far exceed payables 200bn, so growth consumes cash and wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE. FY2025 consumed 100bn on a 139bn revenue increase (-72%); 9M FY2026 consumed 77.8bn on ~224bn (-35%). Base -25% of the revenue change (net WC ~29% of revenue); in the bear case falling revenue releases WC, which the same sign handles correctly.
inputs.tax_basis: Book effective rate 21.8% FY2025 (101,821 / 468,037, 4578.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:785-786) and 22.7% 9M FY2026 (95,810 / 422,273). Cash taxes paid lag (73,972 FY2025 vs 111,217 FY2024; 88,699 9M FY2026) -- timing, not a structural shelter. Modelled 23% stepping to 24% from FY2030 for Japan's rising statutory burden (defence surtax) as US-sourced profit share falls post-LOE. No loss carryforwards or one-off credits to perpetuate.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: pharma ~72% / nutraceuticals ~23% of revenue), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (non-US operating company) with owner-fcf-adaptations (a1) JPY-built WACC, (b) lease treatment B, (c) NCI charged once in the bridge, (d) matching-asset rule for stripped finance income and equity-method profit, (e) SBC-zero market, (f) risk charged once. No prior DCF or memory entry; fresh build. BASIS: FY0 = FY2026 guidance (see fy0_basis). OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported_fcf 261,910 (OCF 403,579 - PP&E 87,841 - intangibles 53,828, FY2025) - SBC 0 - interest & dividends received 18,756 = 243,154 per the house formula; the fully loaded FY2025 figure after lease principal (24,695) and subsidiary acquisitions (87,279) was ~131bn, which is what the forward build's lease and capex paths reproduce -- do not read the 243bn as the run-rate. MATCHING ASSETS: interest/dividend income and equity-method profit are OUT of the flows, so cash (net debt), other financial assets and equity-method investments are IN the bridge at book. STUB/BASIS BREAKS: FY2014 is a 9-month stub and FY2015 and earlier are J-GAAP; no CAGR in historical_growth spans either. FX: FY2026 guidance assumes USD/JPY 158 and EUR/JPY 185 (above the FY2025 average 149.61/169.18); a stronger yen is a translation risk carried in the bear case, not in the discount rate. Reported FCF in the Metrics CSV is PP&E+intangibles only; the H1/9M FY2026 capex column includes the ~117.6bn Transcend intangible purchase, so the CSV's 9M FY2026 FCF of 124.9bn is not comparable with prior years.
inputs.sanity_check_note: Core EBITDA in this model excludes ~45bn/yr of equity-method profit that the CSV's EBITDA (OP + D&A) includes; an EV/EBITDA check on the CSV basis should add the equity-method investments (374.6bn) to EV or strip associates from EBITDA, not mix the two. Adjusted (SBC) multiples are degenerate because SBC is zero.

bear.narrative: The launches underdeliver: VOYXACT cedes share to Novartis's Fabhalta and Tarpeyo once its traditional-approval label lands, SIMTRIYO is a niche entrant in a crowded stimulant market, zipalertinib stays a 2L product; the yen strengthens toward 140 against the 158 planning rate (a ~5% translation hit on the two-thirds of pharma revenue earned abroad) and US pricing/tariff policy bites. The REXULTI and ABILIFY MAINTENA cliffs then land in full in FY2029-31 (-4/-8/-5%) with only partial offsets, and management keeps buying pipeline (capex 7.5%) to refill it. Core margin falls to 14-15% as high-margin US CNS sales are replaced by lower-margin launches, royalties and nutraceuticals. The business remains solidly profitable and net-cash throughout -- this is an earnings-reset bear, not a solvency bear.

base.narrative: FY2027-28: +6%/+5% as VOYXACT (FY2026 plan 63.5bn) ramps toward a 200-250bn franchise, SIMTRIYO launches in US ADHD, zipalertinib gains 2L then 1L approval (PDUFA Feb-2027), royalties (Kisqali/Pluvicto, +87% YoY) compound, nutraceuticals grow 4-5%; JYNARQUE erosion (-35%) is largely absorbed by FY2027. FY2029-31: +2/-2/-1% as REXULTI US (~80% of a 395bn product) loses exclusivity around 2029 and ABILIFY MAINTENA once-monthly follows, with ASIMTUFII, VOYXACT label expansion (Sjogren's, PMN), zipalertinib and Next-8 approvals offsetting roughly 70-80% of the ~350bn lost. FY2032-36: +2-3% mature growth. Core EBITDA margin 21.0-21.3% through FY2028 then compresses to 17% at the trough (lost sales were highest-margin; cost base adjusts only partially), recovering to 18%. Capex 7.0% charges the pipeline-replacement spend. Terminal: the 15x FCF cap binds (Gordon at 7%/1.5% would be 18.5x), so no re-rating is assumed.

bull.narrative: VOYXACT becomes a USD 2.5-3bn+ anti-APRIL leader in IgAN with Sjogren's/PMN expansion, zipalertinib takes the EGFR exon20 1L standard, SIMTRIYO's Schedule III status wins meaningful ADHD share, and ASIMTUFII plus REXULTI Japan/AAD hold most of the CNS franchise so the 2029-31 LOE is a plateau (+2%/+2%) rather than a decline. Royalty income keeps compounding and nutraceuticals sustain mid-single-digit growth in Southeast Asia and US supplements. Margin holds 21-22% (launch spend is absorbed by scale and the R&D reprioritisation already visible in the 373bn FY2026 R&D guidance), capex 6.5% as organic pipeline needs less bolt-on replacement. Terminal growth 2.0%, but the 15x cap still binds.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% because the FY2029-31 REXULTI/ABILIFY MAINTENA loss of exclusivity is a dated, known event covering ~25% of revenue -- product concentration is the central fact of the horizon, not a tail -- and the FY2026 planning rate of USD/JPY 158 leaves translation risk skewed against the base. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent launches (VOYXACT, SIMTRIYO, zipalertinib) to all succeed AND ASIMTUFII to retain the long-acting franchise. Base 50%: guidance has been raised three times in FY2026 and the balance sheet (net cash, equity ratio ~74%) removes any solvency axis.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
